abstract:
Whisper is one of the current state-of-the-art systems for
automatic speech recognition (ASR), both because of availability
and performance. Recent previous research has shown
that such systems may also be applied to more challenging
domains like radio frequency (RF) speech processing, which
typically faces the additional problem of locating speech
within a time-frequency plane and estimating the in advance
unknown carrier frequency (CF) and sideband (SB) of the
modulated signals. This paper proposes a novel approach for
detecting potentially several speech signals in a wideband RF
signal, providing exact time-frequency positions and speechto-
text (S2T) information. We combine a modified You Only
Look Once (YOLO) for the voice activity detection (VAD)
part with Whisper for the S2T part. The paper in particular
analyzes the VAD performance and the influence of inaccurate
CF estimates with respect to the background noise level
and provides a first step towards an end-to-end ASR pipeline.

abstract: Industrial machine failures are rare and often difficult to label, making unsupervised anomaly detection a practical necessity. This paper studies a lightweight self-supervised contrastive representation learning approach for acoustic monitoring of centrifugal pumps using large unlabeled datasets. To this end, a compact convolutional audio encoder is trained with a SimCLR-inspired objective on proprietary pump audio and a subset of the publicly available MIMII-DUE pump recordings, without utilizing labels. The learned embeddings show meaningful structure, with recordings clustering both by pump station and by individual pump, indicating machine- and site-specific acoustic fingerprints, and some pumps exhibit temporal organization suggestive of gradual operational change. For evaluation, the frozen encoder is transferred to the held-out MIMII pump dataset containing real faults. A simple density model based on principal component analysis (PCA) and kernel density estimation (KDE) separates normal and abnormal sounds. Recall ranges from 63% to 85% across pump IDs at a fixed 5% nominal false-positive threshold. Overall, the results show that compact contrastive audio embeddings can provide interpretable structure in unlabeled industrial audio and support zero-shot anomaly detection, while comparison with the 51.6x larger contrastive encoder AADSCL shows that mean recall rises from 75% to 85% under the same PCA+KDE protocol.

abstract: A diagonal-unloading (DU)-guided spatial binary masking method is proposed for speech extraction with a moving interferer. The method operates frame by frame from a single-snapshot covariance matrix, avoiding multi-frame covariance estimation, which can be unreliable under time-varying interference. Although DU provides strong directional interference suppression, direct single-snapshot DU can distort target speech. To alleviate this effect, a spatial binary mask is built from partial-DU directional responses steered toward the target and interferer directions of arrival (DOAs) and applied to a reference microphone signal. Simulations with a stationary target and moving interferer show robust performance across signal-to-interference ratios (SIRs), signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), reverberation times ($T_{60}$), and DOA errors, although attenuation of spatially white noise remains limited.

abstract:
Laser Doppler vibrometry (LDV) can recover speech from vibrating surfaces with high
precision, yet the prohibitive cost of research-grade LDV hardware $10,000-$100,000
per unit) has kept the field starved of training data, leaving laser-based automatic speech
recognition (ASR) and reconstruction far behind their radar counterparts.
In this paper, we introduce LaserSpeech, a large-scale synthetic dataset and open-source
benchmark designed to close this gap.
Our physics-based synthesis pipeline transforms clean speech into realistic laser-like
recordings by modeling the five principal degradation mechanisms of optical vibrometry:
low-pass bandwidth limiting, frequency-dependent (purple) sensor noise, broadband
measurement noise, Nyquist anti-aliasing, and multipath frequency smearing.
Applied to the 460 hour LibriSpeech (train-clean-460) split, the pipeline yields
460 hours of paired clean/synthetic-laser speech at no hardware cost.
We validate the synthetic data by measuring PESQ, STOI, and Whisper WER on the synthesized
LibriSpeech utterances relative to their clean originals and compare those metrics to the same measurements on real LDV recordings across 2 experimental sessions.
A systematic joint parameter ablation over 18 configurations, evaluated on
1,585 LibriSpeech utterances (4.3h), identifies the synthesis operating point whose acoustic
quality profile best matches the real LDV target distribution across two surface conditions
(Wooden Box and Kappa), and reveals which parameters control degradation difficulty
versus speech preservation.
The synthesis code and the real LDV recordings are released publicly to support research on
cross-speaker and cross-domain generalization and on pre-training for laser-based speech sensing.

abstract: Binaural recordings are inherently affected by head rotations. Usually, information on head rotation is not provided and remains unknown. However, knowing the head rotation can be helpful for speech enhancement or stabilizing binaural recordings. Our previous publication proposed a constraint-based optimization algorithm for blindly estimating head rotations from binaural recordings. This contribution proposes an alternative deep learning-based estimation algorithm. We evaluate both algorithms using real binaural recordings with different numbers of sound sources in a room. It turns out that our novel proposed model performs slightly better while the computation time during inference is strongly reduced.

abstract: This paper presents an open dataset of spatial room impulse responses (RIRs) measured at the Arvedi Auditorium in Cremona, Italy, a contemporary concert hall located within the Museo del Violino complex and dedicated to the performance and recording of string instruments. The measurements were acquired using 8-capsule spherical microphone arrays positioned at 65 receiver locations across the audience area. Five sources were deployed on stage: an omnidirectional reference at the geometric center of the stage, and four directional loudspeakers placed at the canonical positions of a string quartet or small ensemble. For each of the 325 source-receiver combinations, the dataset includes the raw 8-channel impulse responses sampled at 48kHz and the corresponding measurement geometry. An acoustic characterization of the hall is provided in terms of reverberation time and direct-to-reverberant ratio, complemented by a spatial analysis of direction-of-arrival estimation accuracy across the audience area. The dataset is publicly released to support research in spatial audio, signal processing, and music information retrieval.

abstract: Hands-free communication devices and speakerphones are inherently affected by acoustic echo and background noise. To mitigate these impairments, end-to-end discriminatively trained neural networks have emerged as the best-performing approach in research and deployment. While recent advancements in generative methods have provided remarkable results for various speech enhancement tasks, diffusion-based acoustic echo control (AEC) research is still restricted to non-causal, utterance-level processing, thereby not widely applicable in practice. With this work, we are the first to propose low-delay (i.e., causal) diffusion-based joint AEC and noise control models DiffVQE2 / DiffVQE2-S, excelling the so-far state of the art DeepVQE / DeepVQE-S models in multiple objective metrics, and, most importantly, in subjective MOS, respectively. In addition, our models are less complex. Furthermore, we show that a limited lookahead applied to the efficient DiffVQE2-S model allows for an even higher performance. These results have been obtained on the ICASSP 2023 AEC Challenge blind test set. We claim the first streaming-capable, diffusion-based acoustic echo and noise control that excels state-of-the-art discriminative approaches.

abstract:
Binaural speech enhancement for hearing aids aims to reduce
noise while preserving the interaural cues needed for spatial
localization. Although deep neural network-based methods
achieve strong noise reduction, they often distort the rela-
tionship between the left and right signals. In this paper, we
propose two novel binaural cue preservation losses. First,
a binaural reconstruction error loss that directly penalizes
masking-induced distortion in the relationship between the
left and right spectra, providing a more direct measure of
the binaural consistency than conventional separate interaural
level differences (ILD) and interaural phase differences (IPD)
errors as in prior work. Second, a binaural cue loss that jointly
models ILD and IPD to better preserve the binaural structure.
Experimental results show that both proposed losses maintain
strong noise reduction performance and reduce masking-
induced distortion compared to the state-of-the-art baseline
cue loss, while the second proposed joint binaural cue loss
also outperforms the baseline in ILD preservation.

abstract: Location-based training (LBT) effectively resolves the output permutation problem in multichannel speech separation by imposing deterministic spatial orderings. For planar microphone arrays, LBT typically adopts circular azimuth ordering to cover the full spatial range. However, the resulting cyclic topology introduces a discontinuity at the wrap-around point, increasing learning complexity and limiting the effective use of spatial cues. This work investigates this limitation by introducing location-based training with folded linear orderings (LBT-FLOs), which collapse circular azimuths into controlled linear orderings. While individual LBT-FLOs exhibit front–back ambiguity, each provides enhanced spatial discriminability over specific azimuth regions. Exploiting their complementarity, we propose an ensemble-style framework that selects among multiple LBT-FLOs using azimuth-guided scoring. Experiments across planar array geometries and reverberant conditions show consistent improvements over circular-ordering LBT, with robustness to azimuth estimation errors.

abstract: Directional-statistics-based mask-based blind speech separation (BSS) clusters normalized time-frequency (TF) observations from M microphones on the complex unit sphere, without relying on plane-wave or spherical-wave assumptions. Existing methods use separately defined angular mixture models, which makes the effect of density shape difficult to isolate. This paper proposes a complex spherical Student's t mixture model (cSTMM) that connects the complex angular central Gaussian mixture model (cACGMM), complex Bingham mixture model (cBMM), and complex Watson mixture model (cWMM) through the degrees of freedom ν and eigenvalue constraints. We derive a latent-scale expectation-maximization (EM) framework with an approximate M-step based on high-concentration approximation (HCA). On noise-free LibriSpeech mixtures reverberated using measured room impulse responses (RIRs), the development-selected value ν*=1 outperformed the cACGMM-equivalent choice ν=M in all 18 test conditions, yielding a mean signal-to-distortion ratio improvement (SDRi) gain of 0.25dB. The model reduces to the cACGMM at ν=M and approaches the cBMM/cWMM in the large-ν limits.

abstract: Traditionally, hearing-aid speech enhancement (SE) algorithms rely on input-based feature estimation, often derived by a voice activity detector (VAD), to configure beamformers. Yet features extracted from noisy microphone signals can become unreliable in challenging acoustic scenes where users most need help. We introduce a novel paradigm in which the settings of a sound processing system are determined by evaluating characteristics of its output. To demonstrate this idea, we employ an output-based system that selects among a set of minimum power distortionless response (MPDR) beamformers. Although MPDR beamformers are typically avoided due to their sensitivity to steering errors, we show that they become effective within an output-based framework. We compare the proposed system to a conventional input-based minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) baseline. Experimental results show that the proposed system consistently outperforms the MVDR baseline, particularly at low SNRs, in terms of SNR, ESTOI and PESQ.

abstract: Neural directional filtering (NDF) has been introduced as a flexible approach for reconstructing a virtual directional microphone (VDM) with a target directivity pattern for spatial sound capture. Building on this idea, we propose NDF+, which enables joint neural directional filtering and diffuse sound extraction. NDF+ reformulates VDM estimation into two coupled subtasks: dereverberated VDM reconstruction and diffuse sound extraction. This reformulation enables NDF+ to manipulate diffuse components in the final reconstructed VDM output. We evaluate NDF+ under reverberant conditions and compare it with representative conventional baselines. Results show that NDF+ consistently outperforms the baselines on both subtasks, while maintaining VDM reconstruction quality comparable to that of the original single-task NDF model. These findings indicate that NDF+ introduces an additional degree of freedom for diffuse sound control in the VDM reconstruction. In a stereo recording application, NDF+ provides controllable inter-channel level differences between left and right channels by adjusting the estimated diffuse component.

abstract:
Mask-based beamforming is a popular geometry-agnostic approach for speech enhancement, typically applying a single mask across all microphones to estimate the required covariance matrices. While effective for compact arrays, this strategy may be suboptimal for spatially distributed microphones, where signal characteristics may vary strongly across microphones. To effectively capture the spatial diversity across microphones, we extend the mask-based beamformer to a multi-channel formulation, where each microphone is pre-filtered by a separate mask before covariance estimation.
To address time-varying acoustic scenes, caused by spectro-temporal nonstationarity, we adopt a frame-causal online implementation with a sliding window. Experiments with simulated compact arrays and distributed microphones show that multi-channel masking yields a benefit over using a single mask when microphone signals differ substantially, while retaining similar performance in compact arrays. We further demonstrate the robustness of the multi-channel masking approach by comparing oracle ideal ratio masks to blind DNN-based mask estimation.

abstract: This paper investigates sound source localization using two spatially separated compact microphone arrays. For a single compact array operating under the far-field assumption, only reliable direction-of-arrival (DOA) information can typically be obtained, making accurate two-dimensional (2D) localization challenging. To address this limitation, a dual-array beam cross-scanning framework is proposed. Within this framework, a frequency-bin-level fusion strategy is developed to jointly integrate spatial responses from the two arrays over a candidate position grid. Specifically, frequency-domain spatial observations are first constructed for each array using a Householder transformation (HT)-based method, which enhances the representation of directional signal components. These observations are then jointly fused at the frequency-bin level to directly form a broadband spatial response on the candidate grid, from which the source position is estimated. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves consistently strong performance across various conditions.

abstract: In source separation based on short-time Fourier transform, asymmetric window functions are useful for low-latency real-time processing because they can reduce the latency while maintaining better separation performance. However, their appropriate design from the viewpoint of source separation performance has not been sufficiently investigated. In this paper, we propose a method for jointly optimizing demixing filters and an asymmetric analysis window within the framework of independent vector analysis (IVA). We represent the analysis window as a weighted sum of bases, which reduces the optimization of the window function to that of a small number of weight parameters. Then, we derive efficient update rules on the basis of the majorization-minimization algorithm. An experiment demonstrated that the proposed method achieves higher separation performance than IVA using a conventional asymmetric window.

abstract: Bird species classification from field recordings remains challenging due to overlapping vocalizations and incomplete species labels. We study source separation as a preprocessing for bird species classification to improve multi-species detection. Specifically, we employ an ensemble of two separators, FTRNN and TF-Locoformer, both trained with mixture invariant training (MixIT). To address the false positive gain caused by separation errors in separated outputs, we propose mixture-constrained max pooling (MCM), which clips the predicted probability from each separated channel based on the corresponding species probability in the original mixture. The classifier is applied to each separated output and the original mixture independently, and MCM aggregates the predictions into a final per-species probability. Experiments on two real-world datasets show that the ensemble outperforms individual separators and MCM outperforms standard max pooling across multiple metrics, and reveal that separation leads to both true positive gain for present species and false positive gain for absent species.

abstract: Immersive spatial audio has become increasingly critical for applications ranging from AR/VR to home entertainment and automotive sound systems. However, existing generative methods remain constrained to low-dimensional formats such as binaural audio and First-Order Ambisonics (FOA). Binaural rendering is inherently limited to headphone playback, while FOA suffers from spatial aliasing and insufficient resolution for high-frequency. To overcome these limitations, we introduce ImmersiveFlow, the first end-to-end generative framework that directly synthesizes discrete 7.1.4 format spatial audio from stereo input. ImmersiveFlow leverages Flow Matching to learn trajectories from stereo inputs to multichannel spatial features within a pretrained VAE latent space. At inference, the Flow Matching model predicted latent features are decoded by the VAE and converted into the final 7.1.4 waveform. Comprehensive objective and subjective evaluations demonstrate that our method produces perceptually rich sound fields and enhanced spatial impression, significantly outperforming traditional upmixing techniques.

abstract: Neural post-filters are an effective tool for improving the reconstruction quality of audio codecs, and hence, numerous models have been proposed in the literature. In this work, we compare several training paradigms—discriminative training, generative adversarial networks (GANs), score-based diffusion (SD), and conditional flow matching—for post-filtering speech and music, and we evaluate the resulting quality improvements across different perceptual audio codecs. We show that GANs can achieve music quality similar to that of SD models at a fraction of the computational complexity. Since the characteristics of a music signal are relevant for the performance of a codec, we further investigate how neural post-filters behave across different signal types.

abstract: Estimating the number of concurrent sound sources is a fundamental step for spatial audio processing, yet it remains challenging in highly reverberant environments. While recent deep learning methods utilize spherical microphone arrays, they predominantly rely on magnitude-only spatial power maps, discarding the phase information of the incident sound field. We propose SGCT (Spherical GCN-Transformer), an end-to-end architecture that estimates source counts directly from complex-valued Steered Response Functional (SRF) maps. The model projects the SRF onto a HEALPix-discretized sphere, using a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to capture spatial geometry and a Transformer encoder to model temporal dynamics across frames. Experimental results on simulated reverberant scenes demonstrate that retaining phase information and leveraging spherical graph convolutions yields a macro F1 score of 0.919, significantly outperforming classical estimators and magnitude-only baselines, particularly for high source counts.

abstract:
We address the problem of encoding room impulse responses (RIRs) into high-order Ambisonics (HOA) representations from arbitrary and potentially insufficient or incomplete microphone array measurements. This task is fundamentally ill-posed for microphone arrays with limited spatial capture capabilities, such as irregular or sparse arrays, as classical linear methods fail to reconstruct high-order spatial detail.
 We introduce a diffusion-based generative framework that models the statistical properties of HOA RIRs. 
 This enables device-agnostic encoding from arbitrary microphone arrays, potentially unseen during data measurement.
 Our approach incorporates a posterior sampling procedure that enforces consistency between the estimated signals and the measurements while plausibly reconstructing spatial information that is unobservable from the limited measurements alone. Experiments on simulated and measured data demonstrate that our method outperforms linear and neural baselines, achieving accurate HOA RIR estimation up to 12th order. 
 A listening test with binaural renderings, including both simulated and measured RIRs, further confirms that the proposed method yields higher perceptual similarity to reference Ambisonics RIRs than all baselines.
The flexibility and accuracy of the proposed framework open new possibilities for scalable acoustics simulations.

abstract: Adaptive beamforming in time-varying environments depends on the length of the window over which the spatial covariance is estimated. A long window yields stable, low-variance estimates but blurs distinct interference states together, while a short window tracks change but starves the estimator of snapshots. Conventional practice fixes this window through sliding window or forgetting factor heuristics that presuppose a constant timescale of stationarity. This paper instead infers the window window from the data. Under the distortionless constraint, the Capon beamformer is shown, through its generalized sidelobe canceler form, to be a constrained linear predictor, so that minimizing output power over an interval is identical to minimizing a prediction residual. Bellman's principle of optimality then partitions the record into variable-length stationary segments, yielding the Online Segmented Beamformer (OSB). The OSB a causal algorithm that maintains a bank of candidate beamformers and resets its covariance at data-driven change points, with regret growing only logarithmically relative to the best segmentation chosen in hindsight. The selection it performs is a form of content-addressed attention over past snapshots. Experiments in a reverberant moving-source simulation, on the SwellEx-96 shallow-water array, and on a distributed microphone array show that the OSB matches the agility of short windows and the precision of long integration without a fixed prior on the coherence time.

abstract: This study describes an experimental assistive listening device, with multiple stages of spectro-temporal filtering, and evaluates it using acoustic scenes presented via a loudspeaker array. Two stages of Short-Time Target Cancellation (STTC) spatially selective speech enhancement processing, implemented using both an endfire array and a broadside array, were used as spectro-temporal post-filters for a hearing aid signal processing chain. The spatial selectivity of the speech enhancement was characterized by varying the azimuth(s) of either the singular target talker or the multiple interferer takers. Speech enhancement in a range of Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs) was evaluated using acoustic scenes with mixtures of five or nine concurrent talkers. There was a demonstrated benefit for the STTC post-filtering, most notably at relatively low (≤ −3 dB) SNRs.

abstract:
Direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation is a key component
of multichannel audio processing, yet many deep learning
approaches remain tied to the microphone arrays used during
training and generalize poorly to unseen devices. This paper
proposes an array-generic neural DoA estimation framework
using measured or simulated complex directional array trans-
fer functions (ATFs) matched to real-world multi-microphone
devices. The method processes multichannel spectrograms
and ATF metadata with separate convolutional encoders,
fuses the resulting representations through cross-attention,
and predicts source directions using a multi-source Carte-
sian vector output formulation. Experiments on simulated
2D and 3D localization tasks under reverberation and diffuse
babble noise show that the proposed approach generalizes to
previously unseen arrays, including mobile-phone-like con-
figurations, without major performance degradation, while
remaining competitive with conventional and learning-based
baselines.

abstract:
Standard speech enhancement (SE) evaluation relies on
signal-level metrics such as PESQ and SI-SNR. These track
downstream model performance well under additive noise,
but we show they break down under convolutive distor-
tion, where the relevant question is whether the enhanced
signal preserves task-relevant structure rather than wave-
form fidelity. We propose TARG-Speech, a clean-referenced
representation-space diagnostic that projects wav2vec 2.0
embeddings into a linear discriminant analysis (LDA) space
fitted on labeled clean training data of PERCEPT-R, and
quantifies label-wise class separability there. Across the non-
clean condition × processing-state panels in our benchmark,
the Q1–Q4 centroid distance in LDA space is strongly asso-
ciated with downstream macro-F1 with Spearman ρ = 0.954
over n = 35 panels. As the subspace comes from a dis-
joint speaker-independent partition, this association is out-
of-sample. The comparison is two-regime: under additive
noise PESQ, STOI and SI-SNR match or beat it, whereas
under reverberation STOI and SI-SNR become uninforma-
tive (−0.333, 0.048), PESQ retains no significant association
(0.476), and only the geometry remains significantly associ-
ated with downstream performance (0.952). The same pattern
holds for the binary-label LDA-space silhouette across three
self-supervised learning (SSL) backbones (wav2vec 2.0, Hu-
BERT, WavLM; ρ = 0.929–0.963). The best front-end per
regime recovers 39–50% of the clean-to-degraded gap under
noise but only 17–19% under reverberation, and one system
falls below the degraded baseline under noise. Supervised
by task-aligned clean labels, the diagnostic complements
classifier-based evaluation rather than replacing it.

abstract: Piezo-actuated MEMS loudspeakers are promising transducers for compact audio arrays with a high transducer density, yet their spatial radiation properties remain largely unexplored in the context of array processing. In this paper, we present a modeling and experimental characterization study of the free-field directivity of a commercial piezoelectric MEMS loudspeaker. Angular frequency-response measurements on five devices, acquired over the azimuth and elevation planes, show that the source departs from omnidirectional behavior already in the lower part of the operating frequency range and becomes increasingly directive with frequency. To describe this behavior, a compact planar model is introduced through a truncated Fourier-series expansion of the measured complex response. The identified element model is then embedded into a far-field formulation for planar loudspeaker arrays and validated on a measured five-element linear configuration. The results show good agreement between the predicted and measured array responses, supporting directivity-aware element modeling as a relevant ingredient for MEMS loudspeaker array simulation and beamformer design.

abstract: Accurately reconstructing the sound field inside of a room purely from real-world data is extremely time-consuming, requiring large measurement campaigns. In the past decade, several signal-processing-based techniques have been proposed to predict the sound field within a region from limited measurements. More recently, data-driven methods have also been proven to be powerful tools for this task. In this work, SFR3 (Sound Field Reconstruction via Repeated Refinement) is proposed, based on an existing diffusion image super-resolution model, which reconstructs the sound field from a grid of uniformly spaced microphones, in contrast to the randomized distribution assumed by several state-of-the-art techniques. The model's performance is compared to a naive baseline consisting of a bicubic interpolation, a kernel-based method commonly used for this task, and a data-driven approach using a complex-valued U-Net, showing that the proposed method outperforms, in terms of normalized mean squared error, the aforementioned techniques, especially at lower frequencies.

abstract: This paper describes joint separation and tracking of multiple moving speakers using distributed microphone arrays and cameras. A promising approach is to use a spatially-regularized extension of multichannel nonnegative matrix factorization (MNMF), a blind source separation method, that allows the spatial covariance matrices (SCMs) of speakers to vary over time according to inertial trajectory priors. This audio-only method, however, typically fails to track speakers when they are silent. To overcome this limitation, we extend the model to a unified audio-visual probabilistic model for reliability-aware integration of visual cues. More specifically, our method treats the 2D position of each speaker, estimated from camera images by a pretrained object detector (YOLO), as a noisy observation. The visual likelihood is a Gaussian mixture on the 2D image plane centered at the projection of the 3D speaker position, with two components representing inlier and outlier position estimates, respectively. The audio signals, time-varying SCMs, and speaker positions are jointly estimated under the maximum-a-posteriori principle, while inferring the reliability of object detection. Experiments on simulated audio-visual data of two moving speakers with crossing trajectories showed that the proposed method achieved successful separation and tracking in the challenging scenario where the audio-only and cascade baselines failed.

abstract: Image-source-method (ISM)-based room impulse response (RIR) simulation is a useful and physically interpretable tool for acoustic scene modeling, but full-order ISM becomes computationally expensive as the reflection order and room complexity increase. We propose a physics-guided framework for fast RIR simulation that preserves the geometric structure of ISM while learning to retain only acoustically important image-source paths during online traversal. To recover energy removed by pruning, the proposed PathRIR uses a lightweight compensation multilayer perceptron to predict the missing late-tail energy envelope and generate a compensation tail whose energy follows that envelope. Experiments on irregular 3D rooms show that PathRIR reduces image-source computation and improves runtime efficiency over a full-order ISM simulator, while achieving low waveform- and decay-related errors. Ablation results show that adding the compensation tail improves waveform fidelity and reduces energy-decay-curve error, reverberation-time error, and direct-to-reverberant-ratio error, with modest runtime overhead.

abstract:
We propose a deep unfolded Recursive EM (REM) network for
robust tracking of a single moving speaker in mild reverberant
environments. Unlike classical REM algorithms, which rely on
fixed-step-size decay schedules, the proposed architecture learns
an adaptive update policy by unfolding the iterative procedure
into differentiable layers. We introduce a Step Size Network that
leverages Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) and Positional
Encoding (PE) to dynamically adjust the recursion weights based
on temporal context and convergence state. Experimental results for
tracking a single speaker under reverberant conditions demonstrate
that the proposed unfolded network outperforms the classical Cappé
and Moulines REM (CREM) baseline, which employs a spatial
grid search to map the estimated centroids to physical positions. In
the single-speaker tracking task, the proposed method achieves a
lower Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) than the CREM baseline,
highlighting its potential for dynamic acoustic scenarios.

abstract: Mask-based speech enhancement is widely used for suppressing noise and interference, but its performance in spatial audio algorithms with multichannel output has not been studied extensively. In such settings, speech enhancement must improve speech quality while preserving spatial cues that are essential for localization, spatial awareness, and spatial release from masking. In this work, we systematically compare time–frequency masking applied to three signal representations: microphone signals, beamformer outputs, and Ambisonics signals. Performance is evaluated in terms of speech quality, intelligibility, binaural cue preservation, and reverberation preservation. Results reveal a clear trade-off between enhancement and spatial fidelity: beamformer-domain masking achieves the highest speech enhancement scores, while Ambisonics-domain masking better preserves the spatial attributes of the residual interference. All methods preserve the target's localization cues.

abstract: This work presents a multi-task framework using spiking architectures for sound source localization and detection. Our approach uses a dual-feature stream, processing Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) for Sound Identification (SID) and Generalized Cross-Correlation (GCC) features for Angle-of-Arrival (AoA) estimation. We explore recurrent and convolutional Spiking Neural Network (SNN) designs trained with a unified multi-task loss (MTL). Our proposed recurrent SNN achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of <2° on the localization task, outperforming the baseline with single injections. Furthermore, we demonstrate the capability of our networks to generalize to complex audio scenes with multiple non-overlapping sources.

abstract: Discrete tokens obtained from neural audio codecs (NACs) have been used as compact representations in audio generation and understanding models. In such token-based systems, token temporal resolution (TTR), defined as the time interval between adjacent token frames, is important because it controls the trade-off between representing rapid acoustic events and reducing token-sequence length. However, most NACs are trained at a single TTR and require separate training for each TTR. This paper proposes a mechanism that enables a single NAC to operate at multiple TTRs using sampling-frequency-independent convolutional layers. The mechanism regards TTR as the sampling period of the token sequence and generates TTR-dependent convolutional kernels from a shared parameter set, while adjusting the stride and kernel size for each TTR. We incorporate the mechanism into Descript Audio Codec (DAC), leaving the quantizer unchanged. Experiments on environmental sound reconstruction show that the proposed model outperforms a single-model baseline that switches TTR-specific layers for each TTR.

abstract: This paper proposes a sequential optimization framework for joint localization of microphones and sound sources based on Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) observations. Conventional batch optimization methods simultaneously estimate all microphone and source positions, making the optimization highly sensitive to initialization due to the high dimensionality of the search space. In large-scale environments, the optimization process may converge to undesirable local or mirror solutions, resulting in severe estimation errors. To address this issue, the proposed method first selects a small set of reference microphones based on geometric consistency derived from TDOA observations and constructs a stable small-scale estimation core. The estimation target is then progressively expanded using asymptotic approximation and sequential numerical optimization. This sequential initialization strategy allows each optimization stage to start near the global optimum and effectively suppresses estimation failures caused by poor initialization. Numerical simulations were conducted for large-scale joint localization involving 30 microphones and 20 sound sources, and the proposed method was compared with a conventional batch optimization approach. The results demonstrated that the proposed framework maintains comparable median estimation accuracy while significantly suppressing large outliers in the 95th percentile statistics. Furthermore, stable localization performance was achieved under noisy conditions without substantially increasing the computational cost.

abstract: Simulated room impulse responses (RIRs), often generated via the image source method (ISM), are widely used in audio signal processing as scalable alternatives to resource-intensive measurements. However, a systematic acoustic and perceptual gap persists between simulated and measured RIRs, mainly due to phenomena such as diffraction, scattering, and device-specific influences that most geometric simulators neglect. Moreover, no automated tool exists to distinguish these RIRs. We introduce RIR-SoM (RIR Simulated-or-Measured), a compact residual network that classifies RIR waveforms via discriminative embeddings. Trained on measured and ISM-generated RIRs, RIR-SoM is evaluated on unseen rooms and unseen simulation methods, including different ISM reflection orders, a wave-based simulator, and device response augmentation. RIR-SoM separates ISM-simulated from measured RIRs almost perfectly, with progressively lower separability for other held-out datasets. An embedding analysis shows that simulated and measured datasets occupy distinct regions of the learned representation, and a saliency analysis localizes the temporal regions associated with measured-label decisions.

abstract: Reverberation can severely degrade speech signals captured by microphones in a room. A popular dereverberation algorithm is the weighted prediction error (WPE) algorithm. When considering spatially distributed microphones, a similar dereverberation performance may be achieved using WPE with only a subset of all available microphones. In this paper, we propose a WPE microphone subset selection method using a novel block-swap subset selection algorithm. The proposed method performs a local search using an efficient computation of the WPE microphone subset selection cost. Experimental results using noisy reverberant speech recorded by 18 spatially distributed microphones show that the proposed microphone subset selection method yields frequency-independent and frequency-dependent subsets with a similar dereverberation performance to that of the optimal subsets computed using exhaustive search.

abstract:
This paper describes audio-visual indoor scene analysis aiming to estimate the speech signals and 3D shapes of an arbitrary number of speakers from a multichannel mixture and multi-view images. An existing vision-driven approach to this task uses 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) for visual scene reconstruction, followed by a spatially-regularized multichannel nonnegative matrix factorization (MNMF) for source separation, with the 3D Gaussians treated as sound-emitting primitives. This cascade approach critically relies on clustering the estimated primitives into an appropriate number of speakers for MNMF in advance, making the whole pipeline suboptimal. To overcome this limitation, we propose a statistical framework for joint source separation and shape estimation through primitive clustering, in which the audio and visual modalities mutually
inform each other. Specifically, we formulate a unified hierarchical probabilistic model comprising visual and audio likelihoods based on 3DGS and MNMF with a shared prior based on an infinite Gaussian mixture model that jointly defines the primitive positions and source assignments. All parameters are jointly estimated under a maximum-a-posteriori principle, with the effective number of sources automatically determined. Experiments with up to four speakers showed stable separation as the source count increased.

abstract: We propose a fully differentiable end-to-end (E2E) generalized echo and interference cancellation (GEIC) backend that unrolls a generalized sidelobe canceller (GSC) decomposition in beamformer (BF)-to-acoustic echo canceller (AEC) processing order. The system comprises mask-driven steering tracking, a null-space projection blocking matrix, and dual-branch adaptation consistent with the convolutive transfer function (CTF) model using normalized least mean squares (NLMS). A single gated recurrent unit (GRU) controller jointly predicts per-frequency step-size numerators, error-coupling gates, and activity masks, replacing all heuristic update control with learned optimization. Experiments under matched settings show that the proposed system substantially outperforms a strong E2E cascade-solve baseline in perceptual speech quality (PESQ) and signal-to-distortion ratio (SI-SDR) during double-talk, at near-parity echo return loss enhancement (ERLE). Ablation shows this large PESQ gain at near-parity ERLE is the principled outcome of joint component-loss minimization—inverting the classical PESQ-vs-ERLE postfilter trade-off entrenched by pipeline-isolated tuning.

abstract: This article revises informed independent vector extraction (iIVE) as a framework for connecting model-based blind source extraction (BSE) with deep learning. We introduce the contrast function for iIVE, which is derived by extending IVE with beamforming-based constraints, enabling an interpretable use of reference signals. We also show that structured mixing models implementing physical knowledge can be integrated, which is demonstrated by two far-field models. With the contrast functions, rapidly converging second-order algorithms are developed, whose performance is first verified through simulations. In the experimental part, we refine iIVE by training models containing unrolled iterations of the developed algorithm. The resulting structures achieve performance comparable to state-of-the-art networks while requiring two orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters and exhibiting strong generalization to unseen conditions.

abstract: Ambisonics is a format for representing 3D sound fields, widely used in audio applications such as immersive spatial sound capturing and virtual reality. Accurately capturing Ambisonics signals with small or irregular microphone arrays is challenging, and deep neural networks (DNNs) have recently been used for this task. However, existing approaches often do not perform well in reverberant environments or poorly preserve the required inter-channel dependencies. In this work, we adapt a long short-term memory-based DNN, originally proposed for neural directional filtering, and apply it to first-order Ambisonics encoding. To address the limitations of previous approaches, we introduce a loss function motivated by the inter-channel structure of Ambisonics signals. Compared with an existing U-Net-based approach, the proposed method achieves a more accurate inter-channel coherence and lower magnitude error, with a slight tradeoff in magnitude error induced by the coherence-aware loss.

abstract:
Acoustic scene analysis is essential for adapting hearing-aid
signal processing algorithms to the current listening environment.
However, state-of-the-art (SOTA) systems typically
rely on multiple independent estimators for tasks such
as scene classification, Voice Activity Detection (VAD), or
Signal-to-Noise Ratio estimation, which increases computational
complexity and fails to exploit dependencies between
related tasks. To address this problem, we propose a unified
and interpretable acoustic scene representation by decomposing
the observed mixture spectrum into speech, music, and
noise power components. This is motivated by the typical listening
targets of hearing-aid users. In particular, we estimate
time- and frequency-dependent power proportions by a causal
low-complexity Deep Neural Network, from which multiple
downstream acoustic scene analysis measures can in principle
be derived by simple post-processing. In this work, we

abstract: Single-channel speaker distance estimation has recently achieved centimeter-level accuracy in simulated environments, yet it remains unclear which components of the room impulse response (RIR) the model exploits and how performance depends on the recording conditions. In this work, we decompose simulated RIRs into four variants (full, direct-only, no-late, and no-early) using the mixing time estimated from the echo density function as the boundary between early reflections and late reverberation. We define four calibration scenarios, from fully calibrated (synchronised capture, known source level) to fully uncalibrated (arbitrary onset, unknown level), and evaluate all combinations on a matched dataset. Results show that without time calibration, mean absolute error (MAE) increases to $1.29$\,m and the model extracts reverberation-based cues, with early reflections emerging as the most informative component. Further analysis against DRR, $C_{50}$, and $T_{60}$ confirms that estimation accuracy improves with stronger early energy and degrades in highly reverberant environments. When time calibration is available, the model achieves a MAE of $0.14$\,m by extracting the propagation delay alone, regardless of the RIR content.

abstract: Spatial target speaker extraction isolates a desired speaker’s voice from a mixture of multiple speakers using spatial information, such as the direction of arrival (DoA). Although recent deep neural network-based discriminative methods have shown significant performance improvements, the potential of generative approaches, such as generative adversarial networks (GAN), remains largely unexplored for this problem. To the best of our knowledge, we propose the first GAN-based method that leverages spatial information to generate the target speaker’s speech. Additionally, by conditioning the GAN on intermediate features from a discriminative spatial filtering model, along with the DoA, we enable steerable target speaker extraction with a spatial resolution of 5◦, outperforming state-of-the-art discriminative methods in both objective and subjective metrics.

abstract: Multi-channel speech enhancement for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted microphone arrays is challenging due to the severe rotor ego-noise. To suppress ego-noise while preserving speech intelligibility, we propose a lifting-based U-Net that replaces interpolation-based resampling with an invertible lifting analysis-synthesis scheme inspired by the discrete wavelet transform. To improve speech intelligibility at extremely low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, we train the model with a hybrid objective that combines a sample-wise mean-square error loss and a differentiable extended short-time objective intelligibility loss. Experiments on a real multi-channel UAV dataset show that the proposed learnable lifting model achieves competitive enhancement performance with a compact model size in the most severe input SNR range from -30 to -20 dB, while maintaining competitive perceptual quality, intelligibility-related performance, and spatial cue preservation.

abstract: Language model (LM)-based speech enhancement (SE) has recently emerged rapidly using latent space features of neural audio codecs (NACs). In this paper, first, we present a unified framework covering six popular LM-based generative SE modeling paradigms based on discrete/continuous latent NAC features: discrete or continuous autoregressive (D/CAR) SE, discrete or continuous non-autoregressive (D/CNAR) SE, discrete diffusion (DDiff) SE, and continuous flow matching (CFM) SE. Second, we are the first to compare their performance in a unified experimental setup and synopsis with diverse intrusive and non-intrusive metrics, enabling a fair and comprehensive evaluation. Third, we propose a fine-tuning strategy with auxiliary losses on reconstructed speech to improve both intrusive and non-intrusive metrics. Trained and evaluated on URGENT 2025 Speech Enhancement Challenge data splits, all continuous-domain paradigms excel their discrete-domain counterparts. The overall best approach turns out to be CNAR. We further show that our proposed auxiliary loss fine-tuning strategy helps to improve DNSMOS, NISQA, PESQ, and POLQA consistently in all six paradigms.

abstract: Higher-Order Ambisonics is widely used to render and evaluate sound fields using loudspeaker and binaural reproduction systems, yet the perceptual relationship between these reproduction modes remains an important practical question. This study compared auditory perception across three reproduction systems: a rectangular 42-channel physical loudspeaker array, a binaural rendering using the equivalent 42-channel layout, and a binaural rendering based on a near-spherical 122-channel loudspeaker layout. Measured fourth-order Ambisonic room impulse responses from nine rooms were processed using two Ambisonic decoding methods, namely the All-Round Ambisonic Decoder and the Higher-Order Spatial Impulse Response Rendering. The resulting responses were convolved with anechoic Japanese speech to generate stimuli, which were evaluated by 13 participants. Two attributes were assessed: perceived area of the sound source and speech naturalness. Results showed that perceived source area broadly followed the reverberation characteristics of the rooms, with significant inter-participant rank agreement in all six decoder-reproduction system conditions. In contrast, naturalness ratings showed greater variation across reproduction systems. The physical loudspeaker system showed the strongest inter-participant rank agreement, whereas its 42-channel binaural counterpart showed weak agreement. The 122-channel binaural condition showed higher agreement for naturalness than the 42-channel binaural condition.

abstract: Task-aware unified source separation (TUSS) enables a single model to handle diverse separation tasks by conditioning on input prompts. However, conventional TUSS does not account for downstream task requirements, such as whether the enhanced speech will be used for human listening or automatic speech recognition (ASR). In this paper, we propose a prompt extension framework for TUSS that incorporates downstream task information into the input prompts and switches the loss function according to the given prompt during training, enabling outputs with different signal characteristics at inference time. Specifically, we introduce an ASR-dedicated prompt paired with a regularized loss function that reduces speech artifacts to improve ASR robustness, while the standard prompt is paired with the conventional SNR loss function. Experiments on the LibriSpeech and JNAS corpora demonstrate that the proposed joint-training scheme enables a single model to improve ASR performance over noisy input across a wide range of SNR conditions by selecting the ASR-dedicated prompt, while maintaining general speech enhancement quality when the standard prompt is used.

abstract: Wide-area 6DoF rendering from sparse Ambisonic recordings is commonly addressed by interpolating parametric spatial descriptors rather than the waveforms themselves. This preserves the fidelity of a nearby measured signal and avoids phase artifacts caused by mixing distant arrays. However, existing DirAC-based approaches rely on geometric interpolation weights that do not depend on the acoustic scene observed by the microphones. We propose a lightweight Graph Neural Network (GNN) that refines only this interpolation stage. The known Ambisonic arrays and the query position are represented as a graph whose nodes contain local DirAC features and whose edges encode relative distance and directional relations. The network predicts positive query-conditioned weights over the measured arrays, while the target energy, diffuseness, and direction of arrival are reconstructed by an analytical DirAC layer. Experiments on unseen rooms, unseen speech signals, and unseen array configurations show that the proposed weighting improves energy reconstruction and radiation-pattern similarity with respect to baseline interpolation.

abstract: Neural speech enhancement systems are typically trained with signal-based losses such as the signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) or mean squared error (MSE). Although computationally efficient, these objectives disregard human auditory processing and may penalize imperceptible errors at the expense of features critical to speech intelligibility. To address this, we propose Co-SDR, a loss computed from the basilar membrane representations produced by CoNNear, a convolutional neural network simulating cochlear mechanics. We integrate this biophysically-informed objective into the training of a multi-channel speech enhancement system, compare it against conventional losses and analyze the influence of the number of simulated cochlear channels. Results show that in corporating cochlear processing priors during training directs the network to prioritize perceptually relevant speech components, yielding consistent improvements across objective speech intelligibility and signal fidelity metrics.

abstract: High-dimensional representations of pretrained speech foundation models have proven beneficial for objective speech quality and intelligibility prediction. While existing work on neural intelligibility prediction usually leverages such representations for task-specific fine-tuning, in this work we evaluate the usefulness of such representations for intelligibility prediction without any further training. We conduct a layer-wise analysis of multiple speech foundation models, correlating various embedding distances with subjective intelligibility scores. The results show that embeddings extracted from Whisper speech recognition models are best suited, with the last encoder and decoder layers yielding the best correlations when using the Fréchet Audio Distance. Notably, the evaluated distances outperform classical intelligibility metrics and are more robust than Word and Character Error Rates. Further, correlations improve with increasing size of the Whisper model from which embeddings are extracted.

abstract: Reliable adaptive beamforming is critical for large microphone arrays operating in highly dynamic acoustic environments. In scenarios characterized by fast-moving talkers and interferers, the available sample support for estimating the spatial correlation matrix is often snapshot-deficient. This deficiency, coupled with array imperfections, degrades the White Noise Gain (WNG), leading to severe target signal cancellation. To ensure stable and robust beamforming, an adaptive diagonal loading method is developed that guarantees the WNG remains strictly within specified bounds. By leveraging the Kantorovich inequality, the desired WNG is mapped to a strict upper bound on the condition number of the correlation matrix. Furthermore, the method results in three estimation techniques for the adaptive loading level, ranging from trace-based bounding to exact eigenvalue decomposition, offering scalable computational complexities of $\mathcal{O}(M)$, $\mathcal{O}(M^2)$, and $\mathcal{O}(M^3)$. The adaptive diagonal approach approach demonstrates highly stable beamforming under fast-changing environment states.

abstract:
Scattering delay networks (SDNs) are  artificial reverberators whose parameters are derived from source–receiver positions and room geometry. For cuboid rooms, SDNs yield high-quality reverberation in a numerically very efficient manner.Extensions based on multiple interconnected SDNs have been proposed for modelling coupled volumes that exhibit multi-slope energy decay, but rely on heuristically defined coupling factors and fail to reproduce correct energy decay for large apertures. 
We propose a new topology for coupled volumes that uses only one SDN per room and introduces a transmitting aperture node to connect scattering nodes across rooms.  We redesign the scattering operation using a matrix inspired by Acoustic Radiance Transfer. We further refine source injection and receiver detection weights. The proposed method reproduces energy decay characteristics more accurately than the state-of-the-art coupled-volume SDN, with a median EDC error improvement of 6.8 dB, validated using FDTD simulations.

abstract: This paper studies the capability of an object-centric audio representation to support multiple downstream tasks within a unified framework. The object-centric model is trained in a self-supervised setup using slot attention by reconstructing Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) patch embeddings from a set of latent slots. It is trained on synthetic audio mixtures, which provides controlled multi-source audio scenes. These slot representations are evaluated for the classification, detection, and separation of sound events by training task-specific output layers. On the classification task, the model achieves an F1-score of 0.8, comparable to clip-level AST embeddings which achieve 0.7. For sound event detection, it reaches a macro F1-score of 0.7, outperforming clip-level AST embeddings at 0.4 and matching AST patch embeddings at 0.7, which encode finer time–frequency information. In source separation, it achieves an SI-SDR improvement (SI-SDRi) of 18.4 dB. Furthermore, in a zero-shot source separation setting, the model achieves an SI-SDRi of 14.5 dB. These results demonstrate that slot-based representations capture transferable and compositional structure in audio scenes, enabling generalization across tasks and datasets.

abstract: Despite advances in cochlear implant (CI) technology, music enjoyment remains a significant challenge for most CI users. To facilitate music listening in CI-mediated hearing, music processing algorithms have been proposed, which reduce the perceived complexity of music pieces. As these algorithms rely on a multitude of signal processing parameters, finding suitable and possibly genre-specific settings can be a tedious process. Therefore, in this study, we propose and evaluate an interactive optimization scheme for parametric music processing algorithms. To minimize the burden on CI users, the process was divided into two phases: first, normal-hearing (NH) participants evaluated a wide range of random parameter combinations using a vocoder-based CI simulation. Then, CI users participated in shorter, focused optimization sessions to refine these parameters. For comparison, we also conducted parallel listening sessions with NH listeners using the vocoder simulation. We tested the approach using a parametric music remixing algorithm that had previously been validated with a hand-crafted parameter setting found through expert knowledge. Starting from completely randomized initial settings, the method was able to find optimized parameter values through interactive user feedback. Both groups, CI listeners and NH listeners using a CI simulation, significantly preferred the optimized remixes over unprocessed music, while for CI listeners, the preference for the optimized settings was on par with the hand-crafted setting. NH listeners using the CI simulation even significantly preferred their optimized remixes. The results of this study demonstrate the utility of the proposed optimization scheme and pave the way for time-efficient, interactive tuning of future music processing algorithms.

abstract: Target-speaker and multi-speaker extraction are techniques for extracting speech from a desired speaker or desired speakers in the presence of other speakers and/or noise. Neural network approaches for this task are often trained and evaluated using simulated datasets, with balanced amounts of target speech and speaker enrolment samples which closely match the target speech. However, in real multi-party conversations, participants are often silent for more time than they are speaking, and their enrolment speech samples can differ substantially from the target speech in the conversation. These factors can impact the training and evaluation of these techniques on recordings of real conversations. This work proposes a new loss function, which helps mitigate the effect of excess silence in training, improving STOI from 0.55 to 0.60, and frequency-weighted segmental SNR from 4.35 to 5.12. Additionally, the impact of the mismatch between the enrolment speech and target speech is explored.

abstract:
Diffusion models have recently achieved impressive results in
reconstructing images from noisy inputs, and similar ideas have been
applied to speech enhancement by treating time–frequency representations as images. With the ubiquity of multi-microphone devices, we extend state-of-the-art diffusion-based methods to exploit multichannel inputs for improved performance. Multichannel diffusion-based enhancement remains in its infancy, with prior work making limited use of advanced mechanisms such as attention for spatial modeling—a gap addressed in this paper. We propose AMDMSE, an Attention-based Multichannel Diffusion Model for Speech Enhancement, designed specifically for noise reduction. AMDMSE leverages spatial inter-channel information through a dedicated cross-channel time–frequency attention block, enabling faithful reconstruction of fine-grained signal details within a generative diffusion framework. On the CHiME-3 benchmark, AMDM-SE outperforms both a single-channel diffusion baseline and a multichannel model without attention, as well as a strong DNN-based predictive method. Simulated-data experiments further underscore the importance of the proposed multichannel attention mechanism. Overall, our results show that incorporating targeted multichannel attention into diffusion models substantially improves noise reduction.
While multichannel diffusion-based speech enhancement remains an
emerging field, our work contributes a new and complementary approach to the growing body of research in this area.

abstract:
Acoustic feedback limits the maximum gain in hearing aids. In addition to several approaches based on adaptive filtering, recently a deep-neural-network-based feedback cancellation (DFC) approach has been proposed, which is trained via an open-loop framework. Since open-loop-trained DFC (DFC-OL) can become unstable during inference at high gains, in this paper we propose an in-the-loop-trained DFC (DFC-IL) that integrates the DFC directly into the optimisation loop. 
This allows the model to be exposed to unstable conditions during training. A two-stage training strategy involving pre-training on stable systems and fine-tuning on a wider gain range enables DFC-IL to learn robust howling reduction. Experimental results on measured feedback paths demonstrate that in scenarios with small gains, the proposed DFC-IL performs similarly to DFC-OL, and both exceed the performance of adaptive filters. In scenarios with high amplification gains, DFC-IL clearly outperforms DFC-OL by maintaining system stability.

abstract: Circular differential microphone arrays (CDMAs) provide compact geometry, full-azimuth coverage, and flexible beam steering, making them suitable for speech enhancement. However, practical acoustic environments often involve unknown desired-source directions and dynamic or multiple interferers. In such scenarios, fixed-null CDMA beamformers are sensitive to steering errors and null-placement mismatch, leading to degraded performance. This paper proposes a circular differential beamformer fusion framework with target DOA estimation. The desired-source direction is first estimated using a CDMA-based steered response power method, and multiple directional-derivative-constrained CDMA beamformers are then constructed toward the estimated direction with different null hypotheses. The candidate outputs are adaptively fused by minimizing the output variance, so that beamformers with lower residual interference are emphasized. Both hard-selection and soft-weighting strategies are investigated. Simulation results in reverberant environments with moving and multiple interferers show that the proposed method improves interference suppression and robustness over representative CDMA beamforming methods.

abstract:
Recently, time-frequency neural vocoders have been approaching
the state-of-the-art quality of time-domain neural vocoders. Vocos
is a notable example due to its efficiency, but its audio quality lags
behind the time-domain vocoders and the reasons remain debated.
Thus, in this study, we revisit Vocos from a phase reconstruction per-
spective. First, we quantify the gap between time-domain and time-
frequency domain vocoders using bandlimited mel spectrograms as
inputs. Later, via an ablation study, we verify the Vocos architecture
is effective for magnitude modeling, but less so for phase. We then
adapt the Vocos backbone to predict phase differences, a precursor
for phase reconstruction, and identify 1D convolutional layers are
hindering their accurate prediction. Our findings indicate that future
research needs to focus on inductive biases that allow the architec-
ture to better model the time-frequency structure of speech signals,
without sacrificing the support for arbitrary input representations.

abstract: Previous work on speech enhancement (SE) based on masked generative modeling relied on discrete token representations of audio signals, obtained using neural audio codecs (NACs). However, a recent study has shown that continuous latent representations of NACs can be advantageous for SE in terms of speech quality and intelligibility. In this work, we propose masked autoregressive SE (MARSE), a unified probabilistic framework for SE based on iterative decoding of masked clean speech frames using continuous NAC representations of speech. In particular, we investigate a set of different decoding policies, ceteris paribus, that is, using the same DNN (a Conformer model), the same NAC (the DAC codec) and the same training setup. The results show that the proposed framework enables a flexible trade-off between SE performance and computational cost. Audio examples and code are available online.

abstract: Reverberation degrades both perceptual speech quality and downstream Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). This paper extends our prior work on Deep Internal Learning (DIL) for single-channel speech dereverberation to a downstream ASR setting. The proposed method trains an utterance-specific multi-scale frequency-band Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) on pseudo pairs derived solely from the reverberant input, requiring neither external data nor pretrained models. We evaluate on LibriSpeech test-clean convolved with measured Room Impulse Responses (RIRs) from three rooms with a wide T60 range, assessing both signal-level and recognition metrics under matched and mismatched degradation-prior configurations. The findings characterise the conditions under which DIL provides reliable ASR benefit and identify prior accuracy as a key determinant of recognition performance.

abstract: Target sound extraction (TSE) aims to isolate a sound source of interest from a mixture, given a semantic query. Existing TSE systems are conditioned on fixed class representations tied to individual sound categories, limiting their ability to handle the hierarchical relationships that naturally organize environmental sounds. In this paper, we introduce ontology-based TSE, a new task formulation in which a single model extracts sounds queried at any level of a sound ontology, from fine-grained leaf classes such as cat and dog to high-level categories such as animal. We propose a learnable class embedding table defined over all nodes of an AudioSet-derived ontology, regularized with a Cophenetic Correlation Coefficient (CPCC) loss that aligns embedding distances with shortest-path distances in the ontology tree. Our experiments across different approaches show the benefit of considering the ontology structure when training TSE systems.

abstract: Noise reduction (NR) and hearing-loss compensation (HLC) are essential components of modern hearing-aid (HA) systems. While deep learning has significantly improved the efficacy of these modules, optimizing perceptual performance, model complexity, and algorithmic latency for real-time edge deployment remains a primary challenge. This study systematically explores the performance-complexity trade-offs across four processing paradigms: (1) a biophysically-inspired HA model; (2) a generic NR model; (3) a sequential Cascaded NR+HA pipeline; and (4) Individualized NR (INR), a unified framework that jointly performs NR and HLC. To bridge the gap between high-fidelity processing and strict real-time constraints, a teacher-student knowledge distillation strategy is employed to train compact, low-latency student models that approximate the behavior of high-capacity, non-causal teacher models. Experimental results demonstrate that the INR paradigm achieves superior HASPI and HASQI scores at a complexity comparable to standalone models, outperforming the cascaded approach while requiring only half the computational cost. Furthermore, knowledge distillation achieves up to 13.7x model compression, though the resulting performance is highly paradigm-dependent: HA models are largely robust to compression, whereas INR models exhibit the most significant performance degradation. These findings provide a data-driven foundation for selecting processing paradigms across diverse computational budgets, facilitating the deployment of advanced, biophysically-inspired processing on resource-constrained devices.

abstract: Legacy low-bitrate speech codecs such as AMR-NB remain widely used in telephony, where they restrict speech bandwidth and degrade listening quality. Coded speech restoration (CSR) aims to restore the speech bandwidth while improving the overall quality of coded speech, but typically without adapting to different speakers. In this paper, we systematically investigate personalization for restoration of speech coded at low bitrates, using a causal, low-complexity Universal Bandwidth Extension Generative Adversarial Network (UBGAN) model as the basis. We propose two personalization methods based on speaker embeddings, which incur little additional computational cost at inference: (i) conditioning a single CSR model on speaker embeddings, and (ii) cluster-based model selection, where multiple personalized models are trained on clusters of acoustically similar speakers. Experiments are performed on AMR-NB coded speech at 4.75 kbps. Experimental results with disjoint seen- and unseen-speaker test sets show that cluster-based model selection does not consistently outperform the non-personalized UBGAN baseline, whereas embedding conditioning significantly improves ViSQOL and WB-PESQ scores for both seen and unseen speakers.

abstract: Wearable devices can help deliver higher levels of interactivity and immersion in audio applications. We present an outline for a system to be paired with such devices that features a separator, a scene analyser and a spatial modification and rendering block, then focus on the separator. With the goal of greater realism and immersion in future applications, we modify the Target Sound Extraction (TSE) scheme to output, other than a mixture of target sounds, a mixture of non-target sounds belonging to classes present in the foreground in the scene and residual ambience. We extend two TSE architectures to the new task and show that the extensions achieve better separation results both in TSE, compared to the original architectures, and in the new task, compared to sequential and parallel TSE applications.

abstract: Conv-TasNet is often presented as a neural time-domain separator, but its design is deeply rooted in acoustic signal processing: a learned analysis-synthesis filter bank replaces the STFT, masking is retained as the separation mechanism, and temporal convolutions implement structured finite-impulse-response filtering. This paper studies Conv-TasNet through singular value decomposition (SVD). For depthwise temporal convolutions, we view each filter as a Toeplitz operator, linking its singular spectrum to the filter frequency response through Szeg˝o-type theory. For pointwise 1 × 1 convolutions, we analyze the evolution of singular values and singular subspaces during training, showing rapid early spectral concentration and progressive stabilization. We then summarize a low-rank factorization scheme for the pointwise layers. On Libri2Mix, truncation near the effective rank gives the strongest compression-performance trade-off, while more aggressive truncation degrades gracefully. These results position Conv-TasNet as both an interpretable signal-processing architecture and a compressible low-rank model.

abstract: Music source separation systems typically extract a single vocal track and do not distinguish between multiple singers. We study singer-informed vocal source separation for multi-singer mixtures. Our framework introduces a short enrollment recording of a target singer to guide separation through a learned embedding. The singer embedding is incorporated using feature concatenation or feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), enabling the model to focus on the target singer while suppressing interference. We construct a duet dataset based on DAMP-VSEP with quality filtering and non-overlapping enrollment segments. Experiments on solo and duet settings show that while baseline models perform well for single-singer mixtures, the proposed method improves target-singer extraction in multi-singer cases, increasing target-singer SI-SDR from $0.33$ dB to $5.58$ dB. Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD) further shows improved perceptual quality and better alignment with target audio distributions. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/jocelynxu01/singer-separation-paper.

abstract: This paper investigates the effect of reducing the number of microphones on noise suppression performance within an instantaneous-estimation‑based spectral subtraction (ISSS) framework employing spectral image inpainting. Previous studies have shown that ISSS achieves effective noise suppression by estimating the noise component through inpainting of the spatial direct‑current (SDC) bin in a two‑dimensional spatiotemporal spectrum using an eight‑channel microphone array. With practical hardware implementation in mind, we evaluate whether comparable SDC estimation performance can be achieved with fewer microphones. We perform a comparative evaluation using four‑ and eight‑channel linear microphone arrays with comparable apertures. Experiments under single-noise-source conditions show that the four-channel configuration achieves noise suppression performance comparable to that of the eight-channel configuration, while occasionally exhibiting improved performance under specific conditions. These results indicate that noise estimation by inpainting the SDC component depends more strongly on spatiotemporal structure than on spatial sampling density, offering insights into compact array design.

abstract: A learning-based physics-constrained neural kernel for sound field estimation is proposed. Sound field estimation aims to estimate the spatial distribution of an acoustic field from a discrete set of microphone measurements, which have a wide range of applications. Among existing sound field estimation methods, kernel-regression-based methods offer a flexible and principled framework for incorporating physical constraints and allow inference through linear operation. It is also possible to adapt the kernel function to the target acoustic environment by representing the directional weighting function as an implicit neural representation (INR) and optimizing hyperparameters using measurements. However, the kernel function is generally optimized for single snapshot measurements of the microphones, which can lead to strong overfitting and poor generalization. We propose a source-position-dependent INR for the directional weighting function, enabling the kernel function to capture common directional patterns and to generalize to unseen source positions in the target acoustic environment. Experimental results indicate that our proposed method outperforms the snapshot-based method by estimating a directional weighting function that matches the directivity of the target sound field.

abstract: In this paper, we propose a proximal physics-informed normalized least-mean-squares (Prox-PI-NLMS) algorithm for acoustic echo cancellation (AEC). The method integrates physically motivated priors on the acoustic impulse response within an adaptive filtering framework by combining stochastic gradient updates with proximal operators. In particular, exponential decay, sparsity, temporal smoothness, spectral smoothness, and slow temporal variation are jointly enforced through a composite regularization strategy, where non-smooth penalties are handled via efficient proximal mappings. This formulation enables the incorporation of structured prior knowledge without compromising the low-complexity nature of NLMS. Numerical results under colored excitation demonstrate that the proposed Prox-PI-NLMS achieves improved convergence behavior and reduced steady-state error compared to conventional and sparsity-aware adaptive filtering algorithms, while maintaining a reduced computational complexity.

abstract: We present a real-time system for computing user location and orientation under constraints of memory, computation, and latency. The system utilizes a set of distributed microphone arrays with independent clocks. It computes angle-of-arrival (AoA) and time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) information asynchronously, and deploys late fusion to compute the maximum likelihood user position. The user orientation is then computed using a model for the radiation pattern of the human voice. We also describe the Cramer-Rao Bound of the estimation, and a deep-neural-network (DNN) based model for computing the estimation confidence. The effectiveness of the proposed system is established using large datasets of real-life recordings under different room environments.
